title: Grain Accounting Bulletin: The Multiple Applied for Work Done by Hand at the Grain Desk
content:
The charge a roll carries on Grain Marketing Contracts is taken at a multiple that recognises who does the work of the instructions standing on the contract.

**Clause 1.** Where two or more signed instructions stand against the contract and no pricing has been worked through the online portal, the charge arrived at is taken at the desk-worked multiple of 1.25, since every one of those instructions is worked by hand at the grain desk.

**Clause 2.** Where pricing worked through the online portal stands on the contract, the charge is taken as arrived at, which is to say at a multiple of 1.

**Clause 3.** Where neither of those holds, the charge arrived at is taken at the single-instruction multiple of 1.1.

## The clauses in combination

| Signed instructions standing against the contract | Pricing worked through the online portal | Multiple |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | none | 1.25 |
| 2 or more | some | 1 |
| 1 | none | 1.1 |
| 1 | some | 1 |
| 0 | none | 1.1 |
| 0 | some | 1 |

Any portal pricing standing on the contract carries it to clause 2, whatever the count of signed instructions; only where there is none does the count decide between 1.25 and 1.1.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A charge arrived at as 240.00 comes to 300.00 where three signed instructions stand and no portal pricing has been worked; to 264.00 where a single signed instruction stands and no portal pricing has been worked; and stands at 240.00 where any portal pricing stands on the contract.
